decisions.reason: Boada et al. motivate their Spanish LOAD recessive P86L age-at-onset (AAO) test with [1,2,4,11] and explicitly compare their significant TT earlier-onset estimate (p=0.002; adjusted beta=-1.75, p=0.006) as 'fully concordant with the effect observed in other Caucasian series [2, 4]'. However, reference [2] ('Cell 135, 993-994; author reply 994-996') is a compound citation combining Bertram et al.'s correspondence (10.1016/j.cell.2008.11.030, pp. 993-994) and Campagne et al.'s original-authors reply (10.1016/j.cell.2008.11.031, pp. 994-996). Inspection of the complete Bertram et al. letter main text shows null AD risk across family and case-control cohorts, onset-age stratification at 65 that did not alter risk results, and no onset-age data in the reanalyzed GWAS datasets, with no positive recessive TT-AAO finding reported in the letter body. Meanwhile, the Campagne et al. reply body (and any Bertram supplementary material) is unrecovered. Consequently, it cannot be determined from primary sources whether the positive recessive AAO effect cited under [2] belongs to an unrecovered Bertram supplement, to Campagne et al.'s reply reanalyzing the already-shipped Dreses-Werringloer et al. [1] cohorts (row 201, 10.1016/j.cell.2008.05.048), or to a distinct empirical report.

DISCUSSION
We have provided new evidence for the role of the

CALHM1P86L marker in ADrisk. Infact,wehaveob-

served a trend toward association in case-control stud-

ies and a full independent replication of the P86L ef-

fect in AAO. Intriguingly, both results are evidentonly

when EOAD patients are eliminated from the pool and

when a recessive model is applied to analyses. Tak-

ing together results of the meta-analysis, the previous

AAO results, the lack of association observed in fa-
milial AD [2], and the present results, it is tempting

to speculate that exclusion of EOAD and familial AD

decisions.reason: Despite its risk-null title and introduction as a prior negative case-control replication of [1], the complete primary text of Minster et al. (2009) [4] (10.1002/humu.20989) reports an independent Pittsburgh LOAD cohort (945 cases, 875 controls) in which rs2986017 (P86L) TT homozygosity was significantly associated with earlier age at onset under a recessive model (71.4 +/- 6.1 vs. 73.0 +/- 6.1 years for CC+CT, p=0.034; combined p=0.03 with Dreses-Werringloer et al., noted with a multiple-testing caveat). In the current paper, Boada et al. do not cite [4] merely as background to motivate a statistical model; they empirically test P86L under a recessive model for LOAD AAO in their new Spanish cohort (TT 77.06 +/- 6.06 vs. CC+CT 79.03 +/- 6.01, crude p=0.002; adjusted beta=-1.75, p=0.006), explicitly compare their estimate as 'fully concordant with the effect observed in other Caucasian series [2, 4]', and conclude in the Discussion that they achieved 'a full independent replication of the P86L effect in AAO' across four independent series. Under the codebook's replication-chain rules, Minster et al. [4] is a directly re-tested and compared empirical AAO target absent from shipped row 201.

decisions.reason: Boada et al. cite Li et al. (2008) [11] once in the grouped statement that 'Several independent research groups have observed that P86L and other CALMH1 markers modulate the AAO only under a recessive model [1,2,4,11]. These observations reinforce a hypothetical recessive model for the P86L variant in AD. So, we decided to evaluate this model in AAO in Spanish AD patients,' while omitting [11] from the subsequent concordance comparison ('[2, 4]'). Recovered primary excerpts of Li et al. (10.1001/archneurol.2007.3) identify a recessive AAO association for rs10519262 on chromosome 15 (near ATP8B4/SLC27A2, p=2.09e-6), whereas CALHM1 is on chromosome 10q24.33; moreover, Bertram et al. [2] note that rs2986017 (P86L) was not on Li et al.'s array (requiring proxy SNPs rs2986030 and rs1555823) and that Li et al.'s public genotype release lacked AAO data. However, because both the full text/supplements of Li et al. [11] and the Campagne et al. author reply in [2] are unrecovered, it cannot be verified whether Li et al. (or a reanalysis of Li's cohort) reported a recessive AAO effect for CALHM1 markers or how [11] maps onto the 'four independent series' AAO claim.
